public_metadata.title: Powered On After 1,000FT? 📱🤯
public_metadata.description:
Powered On After 1,000FT? 📱🤯

One phone split at 300 feet, but a different phone powered on after a separate 1,000-foot drop—here’s one possible reason.

#PhoneDrop #TechExplained #shorts

snapshot.evidence_source: User-supplied public YouTube URL inspected with yt-dlp; public transcode downloaded temporarily and checked with ffprobe and frame correlation
snapshot.interpretation: Snapshot was taken 93 seconds after the public timestamp. Zero views at this point is upload-state evidence only and must not be used to diagnose distribution, hook, or retention.

artifact_identity_check.similarity_method: Pearson correlation on 270x480 grayscale frames at identical timestamps, followed by a 2 fps local-time alignment search within plus or minus four seconds
artifact_identity_check.interpretation: The public upload and local exact-final master are the same visual lineage, with near-identical same-time frames through 15 seconds. Later public frames align best to local frames approximately 1.5-2.0 seconds later, so the public 56.331610-second timeline is not the exact 58.000000-second local master timeline. This establishes a timing/edit difference, not its cause. Byte identity, audio identity, and a specific trim operation are not claimed.
artifact_identity_check.warning: Use 56.331610 seconds as the public experiment duration. Do not treat exact-final local QC as proof of the public timeline after 15 seconds without a Studio-side upload check.

observed_packaging_deviations: The public timeline is 1.668390 seconds shorter than the local exact-final master and diverges after 15 seconds before realigning later with an approximately 1.5-2.0-second offset.
No public tags were exposed; this does not prove that the separate Studio tags field is empty.
